description: A second order state variable filter modelled on the analogue circuit, giving low pass, high pass, band pass and band stop versions of one input.

params.text: Sets the corner frequency of the filter, 20Hz to 20480Hz, starting at 261.63Hz.
Attenuates the cutoff CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.
Sets the quality factor Q, 0.707 to 20; with Enable Self Oscilation switched on in the menu the damping is taken out and the filter rings at its cutoff frequency whatever this is set to.
Attenuates the resonance CV input, and inverts it when turned below zero.
Nothing in the module reads this control; the boost CV is applied at a fixed 20dB per volt.
Sets the gain the filter applies to its output, -20dB to 20dB, flat at the centre.

inputs.text: The audio to be filtered; sixteen channels are filtered separately.
Shifts the corner frequency by one octave per volt, scaled by its attenuverter.
Raises the quality factor Q; 10V adds the whole range of 20 with its attenuverter at maximum.
Adds to the boost and cut directly, 20dB per volt, stopping at 20dB.

outputs.text: The low pass version of the input, clamped between -5V and 5V.
The high pass version of the input, clamped between -5V and 5V.
The band pass version of the input, clamped between -5V and 5V.
The band stop version of the input, clamped between -5V and 5V.

notes: the cutoff and resonance CV inputs are each multiplied by the attenuverter beside them, and those start at zero, so a patched cable changes nothing until one is turned up.
menu: Enable Gain Compensation — drops the input by half the resonant peak in dB, so that raising Q does not raise the level.
Enable NLP — soft clips the band pass node inside the filter, adding saturation as the level rises.
Enable Self Oscilation — takes the damping out of the filter so that it rings at its cutoff frequency.
Match gain at Nyquist for LPF — adds a correction to the low pass output that matches the gain of the analogue filter near Nyquist; the other three outputs are unchanged.
